summary:
Jüri Reinvere (born 1971) is an Estonian composer, poet and essayist who has lived in Germany since 2005 and is a Finnish citizen. His music combines modernist techniques with romantic elements, and often addresses history, nature, politics, human perception and theology. He studied in Tallinn, Warsaw and Helsinki, and credits pianist and writer Käbi Laretei and director Ingmar Bergman as important influences on his dramatic writing.

His operas include *Puhdistus*, premiered at the Finnish National Opera in 2012; *Peer Gynt*, premiered in Oslo in 2014; and *Minona*, premiered at Theater Regensburg. Other works range from orchestral and chamber music to poetry settings and the oratorio *The Expulsion of Ishmael*, premiered in Berlin in 2022.

Reinvere also writes cultural and political essays for publications including *Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung* and Estonia’s *Postimees*. His honors include the Estonian State Award in 2015 and the OPUS Klassik Composer of the Year award in 2025.
